items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had met a young man in Chicago who was known as Bob Red Cross

ctx.x: I would pick on a little pot now and then, and before we left for Canada, I had bought six sticks of some stuff known as "Red Cross". I had met a young man in Chicago who was known as Bob Red Cross when I played the Pump Room with Teddy Wilson and Bob was a pot seller who rolled his stuff with an end on the paper that allowed a smoker to get the value of every grain.

When we arrived in Montreal, I stayed in a room with Ted Donnelly and before going to work that night, I put the sticks of Red Cross in a dresser drawer. But after the dance, I met some people who invited me to their house for a few drinks. I got high and slept there until around eight o' clock that morning and when I returned to the hotel, the bus was ready to leave. Ted told me that he had packed my things, so I had a cup of coffee while we were waiting for someone else to come and when we left, we were almost…
